thread.title: Will 2018 Be The Year Netflix Turns On The Earnings Spigot?

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Will 2018 Be The Year Netflix Turns On The Earnings Spigot?
text:
Internet television leader Netflix ( NFLX ) has been investing heavily in recent years to build out its global distribution network and fund original content production at the expense of profits. But this year it could start to show its earnings leverage, a Wall Street analyst predicts.
Netflix's earnings growth will be the next phase of the company's story for investors, GBH Insights analyst Daniel Ives said in a report Tuesday.
"With the company spending major resources over the last two years building out a global distribution arm and customer base in over 100 countries, we believe the fruits of this labor will start to be fully realized in 2018 and beyond," Ives said.
Ives reiterated his rating of "highly attractive" on Netflix stock and raised his price target to 255 from 235.
Netflix stock gained 1.3% to close at 220.33 on the stock market today . It hit an all-time high of 226.07 on Tuesday.
"Our bullish thesis on Netflix is based on our belief that the company's competitive moat, franchise appeal, ability to increase international streaming customers through 2020, and original content build out will translate into robust profitability and growth as the next phase of this story plays out over the coming year," Ives said.
IBD'S TAKE: Netflix stock broke out of an 11-week flat base with a buy point of 204.48 on Jan. 3. For more analysis on Netflix, visit the IBD Stock Checkup . 
Growing competition from the likes of Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ) and Walt Disney ( DIS ) remains a major concern, but Netflix has a big head start in subscription video on demand, Ives said.
"While the landscape for original content has become increasingly competitive with new entrants entering the market by the day (Disney/Fox remains a clear competitive worry), we believe Netflix remains in a unique position of strength to grow its content and distribution tentacles over the next 12 to 18 months and thus further build out its massive content and streaming footprint," Ives said.
Netflix is likely to provide more details on its 2018 outlook when it reports fourth-quarter 2017 results after the market close on Monday. Wall Street is modeling Netflix to earn 41 cents a share, up 173% year over year, on sales of $3.26 billion, up 32%, in the December quarter, according to Zacks Investment Research.
For the current quarter, analysts are forecasting Netflix to earn 56 cents a share, up 40%, on sales of $3.52 billion, up 34%, Zacks said. Investors will be closely watching how many new subscribers Netflix added in the fourth quarter. The company set a target of 6.3 million new subscribers for the period.
It ended the September quarter with 109.25 million streaming subscribers worldwide, including 52.77 million in the U.S. and 56.48 million in international markets.
On Thursday, Morgan Stanley analyst Ben Swinburne raised his price target on Netflix to 255 from 235 and reiterated his overweight rating. He predicts continued strong subscriber gains and earnings growth ahead.
